name: Singapore Management University
feeMethod: Charges one rate for every undergraduate degree except Law, so every major costs the same.
description: Singapore Management University is a publicly funded university established in 2000, with a city campus in Singapore's Bras Basah district. It specialises in business, economics, accountancy, law, computing and the social sciences, taught in a seminar-style format.
whyIncluded: One of Singapore's MOE-funded Autonomous Universities, and the local reference point for business, economics and law degrees that Singaporean students often compare with overseas alternatives.

programmes.name: Master of Science in Financial Economics (MSFE)
programmes.feeBasis: The published Aug 2027 fee for the whole MSFE, spread over the 18-month full-time duration. Self-funded: the same tuition for all nationalities; only the small registration fee differs.
programmes.summary: Programme total (S$57,700 from the August 2027 intake) spread over 18 months, one fee for all including GST, plus a yearly miscellaneous fee that replaces the old one-off registration fee. Not government-subsidised.
programmes.notes: Self-funded programme: one tuition fee for all nationalities, no MOE-subsidised Citizen/PR rate. Official School of Economics MSFE page, 'Programme Fees' table: 'Tuition Fee for January 2027 Intake' S$54,500 inclusive of GST for the whole programme (billed S$21,800 + S$16,350 + S$16,350), with no separate SC/PR column, so the same tuition is recorded under citizen, pr and international; divided here by the 18-month full-time duration (flexible to 12 months). feeYear 2026 covers the January 2027 (AY2026/27) intake. The only Citizen/PR difference the page publishes is the one-off non-refundable registration fee on acceptance: S$400 incl. GST for Singapore Citizens/PRs, S$500 for international students (the page labels the S$500 'exclusive of GST'; the stated amount is recorded); the S$5,000 deposit contributes to tuition and is not counted separately. MOE check (2026-10-01): MOE's Tuition Grant Scheme page (moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/tuition-grant-scheme, updated 23 Jun 2026) covers 'selected full-time diploma and undergraduate courses' only; MOE parliamentary replies of 10 Jan 2023 and 24 Sep 2025 state that only around 20% of master's-by-coursework programmes at the autonomous universities are MOE-subsidised (profession-entry or sector-agency-aligned programmes) and the rest are non-subsidised; SMU's own list of MOE-subsidised graduate programmes (graduatestudies.smu.edu.sg/research-masters/programme-fees) contains only MPhil programmes, not the MSFE. The MSFE page's 'Discounts' section lists only a 10% SMU/SUTD alumni discount and says SMU may amend discount schemes per cohort. SMU's central 25th-anniversary scheme (media release 29 Oct 2024, 'from January 2025 onwards') advertises a S$5,000 discount for Singapore Citizens/PRs on the base fee before GST, not combinable with other discounts, but the MSFE programme page does not list it, its alumni discount differs from the central scheme, and SMU's discount calculator says discounts 'may vary depending on the specific programme', so no SC/PR net fee is derived here; a citizen or PR should ask SMU whether that discount applies to the MSFE. The page states the August 2027 intake fee rises to S$57,700 incl. GST (also shown on masters.smu.edu.sg/msfe as 'from August 2027 intake onwards') and that from AY2027 an annual miscellaneous fee of S$400 (SC/PR) or S$480 (international), excl. GST, replaces the registration fee. SMU's sites block bots, so the official pages were read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-01, hence sourceType secondary. No earlier intake's fee is published live. Fee history: the 2025 rows come from Wayback Machine copies of SMU's official MSFE page on the masters site, masters.smu.edu.sg/programme/master-in-financial-economics, captures 20250529140623 and 20250926112051 (read on 2026-10-02 through the translate.goog mirror of web.archive.org): 'Tuition Fee for Regular Pathway Intake (Jan Term)' S$54,500 inclusive of GST (18-month full-time regular pathway, application deadline 'September (for January intake)') and 'Tuition Fee for Accelerated Pathway Intake (Aug Term)' S$45,780 inclusive of GST (12-month accelerated pathway, deadline 'May (for August intake)'); registration/deposit 'S$400 (inclusive of GST) + S$5000' for Singapore citizens/PRs and 'S$500 (inclusive of GST) + S$5000' for international students; the only discount listed was 10% for SMU/SUTD alumni, so one fee is recorded for all tiers. The page does not print the intake year next to the fee; both captures were made while applications were open for the August 2025 (accelerated) and January 2026 (regular) intakes, i.e. AY2025/26, so the regular-pathway figure is recorded as feeYear 2025 (it is also the same S$54,500 the official page states for the January 2027 intake); the accelerated pathway is not modelled. No 2024 row could be recorded: the Wayback Machine holds only bot-blocked captures of economics.smu.edu.sg/msfe (20240616145106, 598 bytes) and of the masters-site page before May 2025 (20250108191101, 935 bytes), no capture of economics.smu.edu.sg/msfe/fees, /admissions or /faq, of masters.smu.edu.sg/msfe or of economics.smu.edu.sg/master-science-financial-economics; the School of Economics master's brochure (SOE Master Brochure.pdf, also on Scribd as 'SMU-Economics-Masters-Brochure-23') carries no fees; MySkillsFuture lists no MSFE course; and aggregators give only undated figures (topuniversities.com S$43,600 in January and October 2025 captures, shiksha.com S$31,856, hotcoursesabroad.com the current S$54,500) that cannot be tied to the 2024 intake, so nothing was estimated. Second pass, 2026-10-05: no 2024 row. Common Crawl CC-MAIN-2023-50 to CC-MAIN-2025-30 for economics.smu.edu.sg/ (167 records; /msfe/home 2024-08-13, /msfe/overview 2024-11-14, /msfe/skbi_overview 2024-03-05) and masters.smu.edu.sg/ (128 records, no MSFE page): all HTML records are ~1 KB bot-block pages. The Wayback file listing of economics.smu.edu.sg/sites/economics.smu.edu.sg/files/ has no MSFE fee or brochure PDF (only MSFE-Calendar.png, May 2025). Web search finds LKCSB 'your-pg-one-stop' ProgramFee_*_2024 PDFs for other SMU master's (MWM, MIM, MAF) but none for the MSFE, which is run by the School of Economics. Aggregators found (applybuds, unimymasters) give undated figures only. Not estimated. Final sweep 2026-10-06: no 2024 row. Web searches for an intake-labelled 2024 MSFE fee (press, SMU graduate fee notices, SkillsFuture) found nothing new beyond the sources listed above. Not estimated. Unofficial-source pass 2026-10-13: no 2024 row; searches for an intake-labelled 2024 MSFE fee found only undated aggregator figures. Round 5 (2026-10-13): 2024 rows added from an SMU School of Economics recruitment deck hosted by National Chengchi University (econo.nccu.edu.tw/upload/19/doc/31218/PU PPT (En)-updated.pdf; SMU PowerPoint template, PDF created 25 Nov 2024), 'Programme Fees & Scholarships' table: MSc in Financial Economics 'Regular Pathway (January 2025)' S$52,320* and 'Accelerated Pathway (August 2025)' S$43,600*, '*Inclusive of GST'; Application Fee S$100, Registration Fee S$500. The January 2025 regular-pathway intake is AY2024/25, so feeYear 2024 (same mapping as the Jan 2026 intake = feeYear 2025): S$52,320 / 1.5 = S$34,880 for all tiers (no SC/PR rate listed). Marked secondary because the copy is hosted by a third party; it is consistent with official figures (Accelerated S$43,600 matches the undated topuniversities figure; S$52,320 = S$48,000 + 9% GST, below the official S$54,500 for Jan 2026). The deck lists only the S$500 registration fee (its audience is international), so oneOffFees is set only on the international row and the SC/PR rows use the current S$400. Fix 2026-10-15: sourceType changed from secondary to official: the sourceUrl https://economics.smu.edu.sg/msfe is the university's own page, and the notes record that the reader proxy was only the route by which the official page was read, not a third-party source. Fix 2026-10-15: the summary's 'read from a third-party copy' sentence was removed because the record is sourceType official (the reader proxy only transported the university's own page). Source: https://economics.smu.edu.sg/msfe. Fix 2026-10-15: moved to feeYear 2027 (August 2027 intake, AY2027/28): SMU's MSFE page (https://economics.smu.edu.sg/msfe, which now resolves to https://masters.smu.edu.sg/programme/master-in-financial-economics; Admissions tab, 'Programme Fees', read 2026-10-15 in a headless browser) states 'the Tuition fee for the August 2027 intake is $57,700 (inclusive of GST)', so annualTuition = 57,700 / 1.5 = S$38,466.67 for all tiers, and 'From AY2027, the Miscellaneous fee changes to $400 for Singapore citizens and permanent residents, and $480 for international students. Fees indicated exclude GST and are payable annually', replacing the one-off registration fee: annualCompulsoryFees 400 (citizen, pr) / 480 (international) and oneOffFees 0. The deposit rises to S$8,000 (excl. GST) from AY2027 but still counts towards tuition, so it is not recorded. The January 2027 intake (S$54,500, registration fee S$400 / S$500) is kept as the 2026 feeHistory rows.

programmes.name: Master of Science in Applied Finance (MAF)
programmes.feeBasis: The published Aug 2027 total for the MAF, spread over 18 months; Singaporeans/PRs get a S$5,000 discount (before GST), estimated by us. SMU calls the 2027 fee indicative.
programmes.summary: Programme total spread over 18 months, including GST. Citizens and PRs get a S$5,000 discount. Plus annual miscellaneous fees. Indicative fee.
programmes.notes: No MOE subsidy (self-funded programme), but the official Lee Kong Chian School of Business MAF page publishes one tuition fee plus a nationality discount, so the Citizen/PR tiers are recorded net of that discount. Tuition fee S$63,220 inclusive of GST for the whole programme (Programme Fees table); the 'Discounts' section states 'Singaporean citizens and Permanent Residents are eligible for a one-time discount of S$5,000', applicable to students joining from the January 2025 intake onwards, one discount per student (the higher applies if several qualify, e.g. the S$8,000 SMU alumni discount), and 'deductable before Goods and Services Tax (GST)'. Derivation: S$63,220 / 1.09 = S$58,000 before GST, less S$5,000 = S$53,000, plus 9% GST = S$57,770 incl. GST for Citizens/PRs; international students pay the full S$63,220 (an ASEAN citizen discount of S$3,000 exists but is not applied here). Both divided by the 18-month full-time duration (24 months part-time): S$38,513.33 (citizen/pr) and S$42,146.67 (international) per year. The only intake shown is August 2027 (applications September 2026 to May 2027), hence feeYear 2027; the page says the August 2027 fees are indicative and subject to revision. Compulsory fees = annual Miscellaneous Fees for AY2027: S$400 (Singaporeans/PRs) or S$480 (international), excl. GST. The S$8,000 advance tuition fee contributes to the first tuition billing and is not counted separately; application fee S$100 excluded. SMU's sites block bots, so the official page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-01, hence sourceType secondary. Fee history: the 2024 rows (August 2024 intake, AY2024/25) come from a Wayback Machine copy of SMU's official MAF programme page (web.archive.org capture 20240722135036 of masters.smu.edu.sg/programme/msc-in-applied-finance, read on 2026-10-01): tuition fee S$54,500 inclusive of GST for the whole programme (S$36,333.33 per year over 18 months), the same for all nationalities (the only discount then was S$5,000 for SMU alumni, so no Citizen/PR deduction is made for 2024), plus a one-off registration fee of S$400 (Singaporeans/PRs) or S$500 (international) incl. GST and no annual miscellaneous fee; the S$5,000 advance tuition fee counted towards tuition. The 2025 rows (August 2025 intake, AY2025/26) come from the Wayback Machine copy of the same official SMU MAF programme page, capture 20250310171820 of masters.smu.edu.sg/programme/msc-in-applied-finance (read on 2026-10-02 through the translate.goog mirror of web.archive.org; business.smu.edu.sg captures are bot-block pages): 'Tuition Fee (inclusive of GST) S$59,950', application period 'Now to end-May 2025' for the August intake; 'Singaporean citizens and Permanent Residents are eligible for a one-time discount of S$5,000', applicable 'from the January 2025 intake onwards', 'deductable before Goods and Services Tax (GST)' and '9% GST of the discounted tuition fee will apply', so Citizens/PRs: S$59,950 / 1.09 = S$55,000 before GST, less S$5,000 = S$50,000, plus 9% GST = S$54,500 incl. GST (S$36,333.33 per year over 18 months); international S$59,950 (S$39,966.67 per year). Registration fee S$400 (Singaporeans/PRs) or S$500 (international) incl. GST, no annual miscellaneous fee; the S$5,000 advance tuition fee contributed to the first tuition billing (other discounts then: S$8,000 SMU alumni, S$4,000 local autonomous-university graduates, S$3,000 ASEAN; only the highest applies). The 2026 rows (August 2026 intake, AY2026/27) come from a single dated source found by web search on 2026-10-04: SMU's 'Programme Tuition Fees' billing schedule PDF in the Lee Kong Chian School of Business 'your-pg-one-stop' resources folder (business.smu.edu.sg/.../Finance Related/ProgramFee_MAF_2026.pdf, PDF published 9 Feb 2026 per its metadata). It is an SMU-hosted document but not the programme page and was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai), so treat it as a secondary/unofficial-route source. Exact wording: 'Master of Science in Applied Finance (MAF) - FT Aug-26 21-Aug-26,Fri $25,288.00 27-Dec-26,Sun $18,966.00 28-Mar-27,Sun $18,966.00' under 'Tuition fee per Billing (Incl. GST)', with 'Please note that the 1st billing is inclusive of the advance fee' and '*Amounts are based on best estimate and may have some rounding off difference in actual billing.' (the PT Aug-26 row has the same three amounts). The year label is the intake column 'Aug-26'. The three billings sum to S$63,220 incl. GST for the whole programme. Cross-check of the same document series against figures already on file: the same PDF's 'FT Aug-25' row ($23,980 + $17,985 + $17,985 = S$59,950) equals the 2025 programme-page fee, and ProgramFee_MAF_2024_v4.pdf's Aug-24 rows ($21,800 + $16,350 + $16,350 = S$54,500) equal the 2024 fee, so these schedules show the full fee before any nationality discount. The S$5,000 Citizen/PR discount applies 'from the January 2025 intake onwards' and is 'deductable before GST' (SMU MAF page, as above), so Citizens/PRs (derived): S$63,220 / 1.09 = S$58,000, less S$5,000 = S$53,000, plus 9% GST = S$57,770 incl. GST (S$38,513.33 per year over 18 months); international S$63,220 (S$42,146.67 per year). Compulsory fees: the current programme-fees page says 'From AY2027, all postgraduate students at SMU will have to pay Miscellaneous Fees ... The Miscellaneous Fees replace the current Registration Fees', so the August 2026 intake is recorded with the registration fee S$400 (Singaporeans/PRs) or S$500 (international) incl. GST and no annual fee. Fix 2026-10-15: the summary's 'read from a third-party copy' sentence was removed because the record is sourceType official (the reader proxy only transported the university's own page). Source: https://business.smu.edu.sg/master-applied-finance.

The fee includes a non-refundable S$8,000 tuition deposit, which is not counted separately. Compulsory fees = annual miscellaneous fees from the 2027 intake: S$400 (Singaporeans/PRs) or S$480 (foreigners), excl. GST. Application fee S$100 excluded. One fee is recorded for all tiers because the Citizen/PR discount only applies 'from 2025 intake onwards'. The 2024 one-off fee is recorded as S$500 for every tier because that is the only registration fee the 2024 source states; SMU's 2025 page charges Singaporeans/PRs S$400, so the Citizen/PR figure may be S$100 high. The 2026 rows (August 2026 intake; first week of classes 24 August 2026) come from the Wayback Machine copy of SMU's official LLM programme page on masters.smu.edu.sg, capture 20260225094925 of masters.smu.edu.sg/programme/master-of-laws (found via the Wayback CDX API read through web-archive-org.translate.goog, page read through the same translate.goog mirror on 2026-10-04; capture 20260116015151 states the same): 'S$38,150 Tuition fee (Inclusive of GST, for 2026 intake)', application deadline 15 May 2026, and under Scholarships and Financial Aid 'Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents Discount S$5,000 discount off total tuition fees (from 2025 intake onwards)', so Citizens/PRs: S$38,150 - S$5,000 = S$33,150, applied literally off the GST-inclusive total as for the 2025 rows; international S$38,150.
